senses.gloss: ? Kutarārkaka, n. of a yakṣa in Kurukṣetra: Māy 〔57〕; dual dvandva, Tarārkakutarārkakau; division between the two names uncertain, but Tarārkaku-tarārkakau seems implausible. Lévi, 〔p. 97〕, refers to Tarantukārantukayor (loc. du.) Mbh. 〔3.81.178〕 (Calc. 〔3.7078〕), which he calls the name of two yakṣas; but it is obviously the name of two localities (acc. to BR, tīrthas) in Kurukṣetra.

kuta-lipi (or, with v.l., kutana-lipi), some kind of script: Mv 〔i.135.6〕. Senart thinks of reading kuṭa, referring to Kuṭaka as n. of a people, but this is recorded only once from the BhāgP., and seems implausible here. The word seems to correspond to kirāta-lipi of LV 〔125.21〕.
kutupa, m., nt. (Skt. Gr.-Lex. and AMg. id., m.), oil-flask: ˚pam, nt., Mvy 〔9016〕; taila-˚pāḥ, m. pl. (ms. ˚kutapāḥ) MSV 〔ii.141.16〕.

kutūhala-śālā (= Pali ˚sālā; expl. DN comm. 〔369.6 ff.〕 etc.), hall of discussion, in which various opinions are expressed and questions disputed; ordinarily used of gatherings of non-Buddhists: Divy 〔143.13〕; MSV 〔i.221.7〕.
-kutsaka, ifc. (to Skt. kutsayati), adj. or subst., blaming, contemning; one who contemns: apamārgaka- (q.v.)-kutsakā(ḥ) Mv 〔i.176.8〕 (prose).
kutsanīya, adj. (cf. prec., and AMg. kucchaṇijja), offensive: LV 〔189.17〕 (vs) mūtre purīṣi svaki tiṣṭhati kutsanīye.
